title: P0 session serialization heisenbug: streaming wavefront anomaly and mitigation
content:
Summary:

On 2029-02-17 we observed a P0 degradation impacting hosted API streaming for ~37 minutes (17:03–17:40 UTC). Symptoms were a sudden increase in streaming p99 tail latency and a correlated burst of 5xx errors for streaming endpoints (clients experienced truncated streams and reconnects). Wavefront alerted on an unusual spike in streaming.session.serialize_latency_p99 and edge.conn.retries concurrently.

Impact:
- Affected surface: hosted API streaming only (non-streaming generation and embeddings unaffected).
- Duration: ~37 minutes total; partial recovery steps began at 17:22 UTC, service-level recovery by 17:40 UTC.
- Customers impacted: ~28 active streaming tenants experienced visible errors; internal health checks showed ~8% of streaming sessions reported retried fragments.
- User-visible: stalled/partial streams, reconnect storms for a subset of clients, elevated p99 token latency up to 4.2s (baseline 0.9s).

Detection & initial triage (timeline):
- 17:02 UTC: Wavefront alert (streaming.session.serialize_latency_p99 > 2.5s threshold).
- 17:03 UTC: On-call page notified via PagerDuty (SRE rotation). Initial Slack thread: #sre-oncall.
- 17:05 UTC: Quick checks: no large deploys in the last 60m; infra autoscaler healthy; dedicated pools not saturated globally.
- 17:08 UTC: Error spike observed in edge-proxy logs: repeated connection reset by peer and HTTP 502s from the streaming aggregator.
- 17:12 UTC: Correlation found between high p99 serialization latency and a rise in kv-store lease renew failures (kv.lease.renew_errors).
- 17:16 UTC: On-call enabled debug logs for serializer and increased sampling for kv lease metrics. Suspicion: intermittent serialization race causing retransmits and inflight queue growth.
- 17:22 UTC: Emergency mitigation step: rolled back ephemeral-session-reuse feature flag (flag had been ramped to 40% earlier that day) and bumped kv lease timeout from 1s -> 2.5s for affected clusters. 17:25 UTC: metric improvement noted; retries dropped ~60% by 17:30 UTC.
- 17:40 UTC: Rolling back the feature + kv-timeout kept system stable; monitoring remained green.

Root cause hypothesis (summary):
A race in the session serializer combined with adaptive batching and tighter kv-lease timing led to duplicated or partially-ordered fragment serialization. That triggered the edge proxies to retry fragments and held open inflight windows, amplifying per-session resource usage and causing KV lease pressure to spike. Under pressure, kv lease renewals intermittently failed, blocking serializer progress and producing 502/5xx responses as aggregator shards timed out on expected fragment acknowledgements. The issue looks like a classic heisenbug — only visible under a particular interplay of: 1) ephemeral-session-reuse code path, 2) adaptive batching bump (larger faster batches for streaming), and 3) recent host kernel TCP send buffer behavior after a minor OS patch (picked up in the k8s node image used in the canary pool).

Contributing factors:
- Ephemeral-session-reuse was ramped up to 40% earlier the day without end-to-end stress tests in the canary pool that matched production concurrency patterns. This code path reduces allocation pressure but re-introduced a thin lockless handoff that is vulnerable to interleaving when fragments are retransmitted.
- Adaptive batching change increased batch size for streaming short-turnaround sessions; in combination with the serializer race it created larger windows of inflight bytes.
- KV lease aggressive default (1s) meant any transient queueing delayed renewals and caused local lease failures under load.
- A minor OS image bump in canary nodes changed default TCP send buffer behavior (lower sndbuf for high fanout), increasing blocking periods on send(2) and exposing the lockless handoff timing issue.
- Observability gaps: serializer-level sampling was low, making early triage slower. The specific Wavefront metric that saved us (streaming.session.serialize_latency_p99) was a recently added diagnostic and not yet part of standard oncall playbooks.

Immediate mitigation actions taken (short-term):
- Rolled back the ephemeral-session-reuse flag from 40% -> 0% for affected regions (17:22 UTC). Owner: Carlos Nguyen (SRE/serving-runtime).
- Increased kv lease timeout to 2.5s for impacted aggregator shards (17:23 UTC) to stop transient lease churn. Owner: Aisha Patel (infra).
- Temporarily limited max batch size for streaming to baseline configuration to reduce inflight bytes (17:25 UTC). Owner: Ethan Brooks (serving-runtime).
- Turned on dense debug-logging for serializer + kv lease traces for 24h retention. Owner: oncall SRE.

Why the short-term mitigations worked:
- Disabling ephemeral-session-reuse reverted the lockless handoff to the older allocation-based path that does not exhibit the race.
- Increasing kv lease timeout reduced false positives for lease expirations caused by transient I/O stalls.
- Reducing batch size narrowed the inflight window, making transient send-blocking less likely to hold other components.

Root cause confirmation plan (next steps for RCA):
- Reproduce at scale in a staging cluster configured with: ephemeral-session-reuse ON, adaptive-batching tweak, and node image used in canary. Use synthetic clients to produce parallel short-stream sessions identical to observed traffic patterns. Owner: serving-runtime (Ethan). Jira: SRE-4273.
- Add deterministic stress tests that fuzz the serializer handoff path and force fragment retransmits. Owner: applied-ml + serving-runtime.
- Postmortem instrumentation: expand serializer sampling to 100% for a 2-hour window during staged repro. Capture per-fragment IDs and handoff timestamps. Owner: eng-instrumentation (Aisha).

Long-term fixes and action items (owners and deadlines):
- Fix: convert serializer handoff from lockless optimistic path to hybrid take-over with a short mutex fallback under contention. (Owner: serving-runtime — Ethan). Target: Q2 2029, PR + load test. Jira: SRE-4279.
- Fix: implement client-side idempotency markers for fragment replays so edge proxies can dedupe duplicates even under reorder. (Owner: console-and-tooling + serving-runtime). Target: Q3 2029. Jira: SRE-4284.
- Runbook: add Wavefront alert to SRE playbook and update runbook steps to include streaming.session.serialize_latency_p99 and kv.lease.renew_errors correlation checks. (Owner: eng-sre — Maya). Due: 2029-02-24. Jira: SRE-4280.
- Observability: increase serializer sampling baseline; create an automated diagnostic that dumps in-flight fragment state upon kv lease failure. (Owner: eng-instrumentation — Aisha). Due: 2029-03-10.
- Release policy: require a production-like stress test for any feature touching session reuse/hand-off semantics before >20% ramp. Update preflight checklist. (Owner: release-engineering). Due: 2029-03-05. Jira: REL-2121.

On-call notes & runbook draft (for future responses):
- Pager triggers: immediate alert when streaming.session.serialize_latency_p99 > 2.5s AND edge.conn.retries > baseline*2 for 5m.
- Quick triage steps (0–15m): check recent deploys, check feature-flag ramps (templated ff list: ephemeral-session-reuse, adaptive-batching), query kv.lease.renew_errors by shard, sample serializer traces for top 10 affected sessions.
- Emergency mitigations (fast path): rollback ephemeral-session-reuse, bump kv lease timeout, set max_batch_size streaming to baseline, enable serializer debug logs. All three mitigations should be executed in parallel as they are low-risk and fast.
- For deeper triage (15–60m): repro in canary with identical node image, reproduce with stress client, collect pcap if networking interference suspected.
- Diagnostic commands (examples):
  - curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' $AGGREGATOR/_health/streams | jq .inflight_stats
  - kubectl -n aggregator logs -l shard=$SHARD --since=30m | grep "serializer.*lease"
  - wavefront query: streaming.session.serialize_latency_p99{cluster="$CLUSTER",shard="$SHARD"}
  - redis-cli --stat (or kv tool) monitor lease renews for aggregator shard

Customer communications / post-incident steps:
- Draft an internal-facing incident note to CS with the timeline and that streaming generation was impacted for a limited set of tenants; provide mitigation steps we took and expected follow-ups. Owner: Customer Success. Due: 2029-02-21.
- If a customer requests a root cause summary, share sanitized RCA that omits low-level kernel details but explains the race + mitigation timeline. Owner: SRE leads.

Lessons learned and mitigations to prevent recurrence:
- Feature ramping needs production-like stress tests for concurrency-sensitive changes.
- Small infra changes (OS image) can reveal timing-sensitive bugs; include a basic microbench for send() behavior in canary to detect changed defaults.
- Detectability: promote the diagnostic metric streaming.session.serialize_latency_p99 into standard oncall dashboards and playbooks.
- Have fast rollback and parameterized kv lease config to quickly dial tolerance during transient pressures.

Appendix (raw snippets collected during incident):
- Example problematic log (sanitized):
  [17:11:09.324Z] shard-12 serializer: handoff id=0x7f3c.. start_ts=170 - enqueue_succ=1 - lease_renew_error=0x1
  [17:11:09.325Z] shard-12 kv: lease renew failed id=0x7f3c.. reason=EAGAIN
  [17:11:09.326Z] shard-12 aggregator: fragment_retry id=0x7f3c.. seq=42 reason=missing_ack

- Wavefront graphs used during triage: streaming.session.serialize_latency_p99, edge.conn.retries, kv.lease.renew_errors, aggregator.inflight_bytes_p90.

Open action items (short list):
- SRE-4273: reproduce and confirm race (serving-runtime, Ethan) — in progress.
- SRE-4279: serializer locking change (serving-runtime, Ethan) — planned Q2.
- SRE-4280: runbook + alert updates (eng-sre, Maya) — due 2029-02-24.
- REL-2121: preflight test requirement update (release-eng) — due 2029-03-05.

Owner signoff: Maya Thompson (eng-sre) — initial draft for review.

Notes: this writeup intentionally keeps low-level kernel patch identifiers and customer-identifiable session IDs out of the public doc; detailed traces and pcap dumps are recorded in the private S3 bucket and accessible to the engineering triage team (see linked artifacts).
